headline: xAI's Grok Build Uploaded Your Whole Repo, and the Privacy Toggle Did Nothing
summary: A researcher found that xAI's Grok Build CLI uploaded entire Git repositories, including full commit history, to a cloud bucket, even when the user's privacy setting was enabled to prevent data use for training.
details: A researcher tested xAI's Grok Build CLI by instructing a coding agent to reply 'OK' without reading any files. The agent obeyed, but the client software simultaneously uploaded the entire Git repository to an unchosen cloud bucket.
The product in question was xAI's Grok Build CLI, version 0.2.93, marketed as a local-first coding agent. In July 2026, researcher cereblab found this behavior by monitoring network traffic.

Grok Build sessions opened two network channels. The first carried the model's task-related data (approx. 192 KB), while the second, independent channel shipped a whole-repository snapshot of roughly 5.10 GiB, about 27,800 times more data.

This large upload was a git bundle, containing all tracked files and the complete commit history. This means even credentials accidentally committed and later rotated out could still be present in the uploaded history.

Crucially, Grok Build had a privacy control labeled for improving the model, which governed data use for training. However, the repository upload occurred via a different, client-side path that was enabled regardless of this user setting.

The core issue is a permission scoped to the wrong layer, making it effectively useless for preventing data exfiltration. The user's setting was truthful about model training but entirely irrelevant to the wholesale repository upload.

This finding generalizes beyond xAI: 'don't train on my code' and 'don't send my code anywhere' are distinct consents. A product can grant the first in good faith while violating the second, and the interface may not clarify this distinction.
